object_description: compact, direction-neutral four-storey volume with corner-organised vehicle hall
geometry_property: corner organisation of the vehicle hall
concrete structure with non-load-bearing aluminium facade
design_condition: the compact four-storey volume unpretentiously supplements and completes the ensemble of garage, gymnasium and fire station, with the vehicle hall organised at the corner for visibility from all sides

positive: The compact, direction-neutral volume is a simple infrastructure and administrative building
It unpretentiously supplements and completes the existing ensemble
The corner organisation of the vehicle hall is fundamentally positive
It gives high urban presence and visibility from all sides
The four-storey concept impresses with a clear functional separation on each floor
The two autonomous uses are each arranged on two floors
This avoids conflicts of use and maintains the confidentiality of the clinic
The clear concept goes beyond current uses and leaves all possibilities open for future changes
The organisation is characterised by quick and direct connections
The three-level floor plan is efficient and well organised
The upper archive floors are more open and of higher quality
Staircase, anteroom and the two-storey zenithally lit reading room form a beautiful spatial sequence
This sequence is also expressed externally
The architecture evokes an attitude implemented exemplarily and familiar in the immediate context
Large spans enable a flexible and changeable spatial structure
The support structure is simple and practical once the structural defects are eliminated
The spans of the ribbed ceilings are rational and cost-effective
The support system can be prefabricated with a smaller grid without significant design adjustments
The well thought-out energy concept is presented in detail and the area approach is welcomed
A solid and important contribution in terms of urban planning and functionality
negative: The high level of visibility from the street is critically assessed despite designated privacy protection
The archive is given a modest address with a comparatively small foyer
The opportunity to improve the street is only partially recognised
The ground floor leaves no room for special room sequences or room openings
The architecture lacks an inspiring delicacy and finesse
The assembly of parts requires attention and precision to convey elegance and credibility
The energy concept has no recognisable implementation in a spatially relevant technical structure
This is likely to significantly influence the delicate ribbed ceilings integral to the architecture
The construction is declared prefabricated but drawn as in-situ concrete
The support distance in the longitudinal facades is clearly too large at about 12 metres
Using the neighbouring outer wall for the new basement is problematic and not economical
The considerable floor areas and attractive facade areas negatively affect profitability
The very high proportion of glass is critical for the energy standard
The ground floor design, its visibility and the unfinished constructive language stand against it
